title: Germany's Leader Fires Back After Trump Calls Their Military Spending 'Ridiculous'
summary: Have you ever been told you're not doing enough, even when you're trying really hard? That's how Germany feels right now. President Trump recently called Germany's military spending "ridiculous" and "one-sided." He says Germany pays much less than the U.S. to help protect NATO, a group of 32 countries that promise to defend each other. But Germany's leader, Chancellor Friedrich Merz, isn't staying quiet. He says his country is making its biggest-ever effort to strengthen its military. In fact, Germany plans to double its defense budget in just four years! NATO countries have a goal: spend 3.5% of their total national income on defense by 2035. Merz says Germany will reach that goal by 2029—six years early. That's like finishing your homework way before it's due. The argument comes as NATO leaders get ready to meet in Ankara, Turkey. Things have been tense between the U.S. and Europe for a while. Trump has also talked about taking control of Greenland, which belongs to Denmark, another NATO member. And the U.S. went to war with Iran without asking European allies first. Merz even said the U.S. was "humiliated" by Iran, which made Trump announce he'd pull 5,000 American troops out of Germany. So, is Germany spending enough? Merz says yes—and he's got the numbers to prove it.
why_it_matters: When powerful countries argue about money and protection, it can affect friendships between nations and how safe the world feels, which can matter for your future.

background_read: NATO, or the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, is a military group of 32 countries that promised to defend each other if one is attacked. It was started after World War II to help keep peace.
The United States spends more on its military than any other country and often says that European countries like Germany should pay more for their own protection.
Greenland is a huge island that belongs to Denmark, another NATO member, and President Trump has talked about wanting to control it.
Article_Structure: WHO: President Donald Trump and Germany's leader, Chancellor Friedrich Merz.
WHAT: A public argument about whether Germany spends enough money on its military for NATO.
WHERE: The disagreement is happening as NATO leaders get ready to meet in Ankara, the capital city of Turkey.
WHY: Trump thinks Germany's spending is too low, while Merz insists Germany is making its biggest ever effort and will reach the NATO target early.

perspectives.description: Germany says it is making the biggest effort ever, doubling its defense budget and planning to reach the 3.5% goal by 2029, six years early.
Trump believes Germany has been taking advantage of U.S. military protection for years and needs to spend much more to be fair.
NATO has a spending goal that all members agreed to, and while Germany is now working harder to meet it, the heated argument can damage the trust between allies.
